name: ziwei-doushu
tagline: An open-source Chinese astrology chart calculator that does in seconds what takes a practitioner hours by hand.
sentence: Enter a birth date and time and get a complete Zi Wei Dou Shu chart - the traditional Chinese system of 14 stars across 12 life areas - with pattern analysis and classical references.

board.say: Casting a Zi Wei Dou Shu chart by hand means looking up dozens of star positions, transformations and patterns across 12 life areas - it takes hours and mistakes are easy.
You open the web app and enter a birth date, time and gender.
A birth year, month, day and two-hour time window (the traditional Chinese hour system divides the day into 12 slots).
The engine converts your birth details into a traditional lunar calendar date and calculates every position.
steps: Places the 14 main stars and dozens of minor stars into the correct palaces (life areas like career, relationships, wealth)
Calculates the Four Transformations - four stars that shift meaning based on your birth year
Matches the chart against a knowledge base of named patterns from classical texts

board.say: A complete chart grid you can read or share.

outputs.eg: Each palace shows its stars, brightness level (1 of 7 grades) and which transformation landed there
Named patterns from the classical Tianji texts, like 'Purple Star in Zi palace' with the original passage

before: Casting a chart means flipping through tables and cross-referencing dozens of stars by hand - a full chart takes an experienced practitioner 1 to 2 hours
Online calculators exist but most are closed-source, ad-heavy, or require paid subscriptions for the full chart
No way to verify the algorithm against classical sources
after: A complete chart in seconds, verified against 768 regression tests and cross-checked with classical texts
The algorithm is open-source and documented - anyone can audit how each star is placed
Two research datasets (675K charts, 20.4 billion characters of interpretations) are published under a Creative Commons license
uses_note: This is a niche traditional Chinese astrology tool. It has 10.8K stars and 2.2K forks, but documented real-world uses by named individuals are thin.

steps: [Open the live demo](https://metisziwei.com/chart) and enter a birth date, time and gender
Read the generated chart - each of the 12 palaces shows its stars and brightness level, and the Four Transformations are highlighted
To run it locally: clone [the repo](https://github.com/Renhuai123/ziwei-doushu), run `npm install` and `npm run dev`, then open localhost in your browser

footprint.disk: The app itself is a standard web project (under 50 MB installed). The optional research datasets are large: v3.0 is 5.5 GB compressed (33.1 GB uncompressed), v4.0 is 161 MB compressed (56.6 GB uncompressed).
footprint.memory: The chart calculator runs in the browser and needs very little memory. The datasets are for research only.
footprint.runs_on: Any modern browser. To run locally: Node.js with Next.js. No specific version listed.

best_for: Practitioners of Zi Wei Dou Shu who want a fast, verifiable chart calculator
Researchers studying traditional Chinese astrology algorithms
Anyone curious about how Chinese natal charts work
skip_if: You don't read Chinese - the interface and all documentation are in Mandarin
You want Western astrology (this is a completely different system)
You're looking for fortune-telling predictions - this calculates chart positions, it doesn't predict the future

alternatives.name: iztro
alternatives.line: The calculation library this project builds on - lighter, API-only, no web interface

alternatives.name: Metis Ziwei (commercial)
alternatives.line: The creator's own hosted version with AI-powered chart interpretation (the AI part is not open-source)

watch: **Astrology is not science.** Zi Wei Dou Shu is a traditional belief system, not an evidence-based method. The engine calculates chart positions accurately, but the interpretations are traditional lore, not predictions.
**Everything is in Chinese.** The interface, documentation, datasets and classical references are all in Mandarin. There is no English translation.

**The AI interpretation is closed.** The open-source repo includes the chart engine and datasets, but the AI-powered interpretation feature on metisziwei.com is not included. You'd need to build your own.
